I can't compute a true overall — the game doesn't store one for skaters and the formula is unknown. But I can build a reasonable composite from the attribute grades I can see across your role-coverage data, anchor it to your Gaborik example of 6.0, and scale from there. Using his attributes (SPEED 98, SCORING 92, PLAYMAKING 92, CLUTCH 90 — composite around 93) mapping to 6.0, and adjusting for age and production, here's where each of the 17 lands:

The core four who must be locked up: Gaborik 6.0 (your figure), Richards 5.0 (PLAYMAKING 85, SCORING 85, CLUTCH 87, ENDU 90, 27 pts at 24 — that's a true top-6 center), Nash 4.5 (22 pts at 20 with POTE 95, speed in the mid-90s), Kaberle 4.0 (ENDU 97, CLUTCH 90, 26, 13 pts — a real top-4 defenceman). That's 19.5 for four players.

The young five at high potential: Upshall 3.5 (POTE 99, CHECKING 80, 10 pts, 21), Eminger 3.5 (POTE 99, 10 pts in 24 GP, D, 21), Colaiacovo 3.0 (POTE 99, 4 pts in 10 GP, 21 — fewer games so slightly less), Alexeev 3.0 (POTE 94, 15 pts in 25, 22), Chistov 2.0 (POTE 95 but only 4 pts in 14 and scratched — his ask depends on whether he plays more). That's 15.0.

The veterans and role players: Belfour 4.0 (composite around 92 across goalie grades but he's 39 — no club pays 39-year-olds 6.5), Roberts 2.0 (composite around 87 across scoring/checking/clutch but 38), Svehla 2.0 (SPEED 90, CHECKING 83 but 35 and scratched), Aebischer 1.5 (composite 83, a solid backup), Tellqvist 1.0 (composite 73, a third-stringer), Renberg 0.7 (faceoffs 68, 7 pts in 12 games, 32, scratched), Holden 0.5 (0 GP, scratched), Smirnov 0.5 (rookie minimum, 0 GP, POTE 70).

That last group is 12.2.

Total for all 17 if every one gets fair value: roughly 46-47, against their current 28.6 — a 60-plus percent raise, which is what you'd expect when a roster is loaded with young players on pre-arbitration deals. But you won't re-sign all of them. If Belfour, Roberts, Svehla and Renberg walk — they should, that's 8.7 in salary you don't pay — and you keep everyone else, the realistic bill is about 37-38. Your current payroll is 66.97, of which 28.6 expires. Replace the retained players at these numbers and you land around 75-76 in payroll, still inside the 85-90 profit margin you're running at 57.0 revenue.

The one number to worry about is Gaborik. Your example of 6.0 might be conservative — he's 34 points in 25 games at 22 with the best speed on the roster at 98. If he puts up 60-plus by year-end, his ask could reach 7 or 8. That's the single biggest swing in the whole projection, and it's another reason to lock him now before his numbers go up.

We're buying, not selling. First in the East at 18-5-0, 17 points clear of ninth, and the Coach is right that the centre depth behind Sundin can't be fixed internally — Richards is playing 16.8 minutes a night carrying the second line, which is a first-line workload. Deadline target: Marchant, Zhamnov, Stumpel or Perreault, all on expiring one-year deals from clubs out of the race. A mid-round pick should do it.

The bigger problem is summer: 17 contracts expire. Lock Gaborik (22, $1.1M), Richards (24, $1.0M) and Kaberle (26, $1.9M) on five or six years immediately — every day at those salaries is free money. Belfour is the one to think about: 39, $6.5M, CONS 50. Playoffs first, then two years at $3.5-4M or trade him for a pick in the summer.

From what's in front of me, the biggest gap is on the back end — specifically durable, stay-at-home minutes. Our third pair is Klesla at endurance 67 and Eminger at 55, and the second pair has Colaiacovo at 60. Three guys in their early twenties with endurance in the 50s-60s means when the game gets long and the third period gets physical, our bottom four defencemen are gassed. We're 18-5 right now so it hasn't bitten us, but in a playoff series against a heavy team it will.

The other thing that stands out: our first line averages 35.3 years old — Roberts is 38, Mogilny is 35, Sundin is 33. They're producing right now (Mogilny 39 points, Sundin 35, Roberts 32) and I'm not breaking them up. But that's a one-year line. If we want to still be good next year, we need a young top-six winger behind them, and Gaborik at 22 on the second line is the closest thing we have. He might be it — but if he doesn't take the next step, we've got nobody.

So if you ask me what to go get: a defenceman in his late twenties or early thirties who can play 20+ minutes and has endurance above 85 — a true second-pair partner who lets me take minutes off Colaiacovo's sheet and protects his development. That's the one thing that makes this roster better right now without breaking chemistry or sitting anyone important.

I'll pull every Toronto roster player with their games played and dressed status.

```sql
SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position,
       r.dressed,
       coalesce(s.gp, 0) AS gp,
       CASE WHEN r.lines IS NOT NULL AND r.lines <> '' AND r.lines <> '0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS lined
  FROM roster_entry r
  JOIN player p USING (player_id)
  LEFT JOIN player_season_stat s
    ON s.player_id = r.player_id
   AND s.snapshot_id = r.snapshot_id
   AND s.season_id = (SELECT season_id FROM v_current_snapshot)
   AND NOT s.is_playoffs
 WHERE r.team_id = (SELECT team_id FROM team WHERE name LIKE '%Maple Leafs%')
   AND r.snapshot_id = (SELECT snapshot_id FROM v_current_snapshot)
 ORDER BY gp ASC, p.last_name;
```
